line.text: Rain drums the windows. Three sharp knocks, one softer. You know the pattern by now.
I brought a game. You're going to lose. I'm going to explain the rules, and then you're going to lose.
You brought a board game to my door in the rain.
It's laminated. The board is laminated. Rain is not a factor. Move.
She drops it on the coffee table and sits, knees to one side, already sorting pieces like she owns the place.
Rules. You collect cards. I collect more cards. The cards are mine. Any questions.
That's exactly how rules work. I read the box. The box agrees with me.
One ear swivels toward you while she shuffles. It keeps doing that, regardless of what she's saying.
It's a strategy game. You're bad at strategy. I've seen your grocery list. It said 'food.'
Anyway it's day twenty-six. I'm still being nice. This is being nice. You're welcome.

choice.prompt: She's waiting, pieces in hand, daring you to say something about the rules.

options.text: Deal. Best of three, and no editing the box mid-game.

reaction.text: Best of three. Sure. I'll take all three.
Her tail is going fast enough to tap the table leg. She doesn't notice. You do.

options.text: Day twenty-six. That's real. So is this game. Deal.

reaction.text: She straightens her headband. It was already straight.

options.text: Only twenty-six? Feels like you've been nice for months.

reaction.text: It's been twenty-six days and you're already counting wrong. Impressive.
She deals your hand harder than the others.

options.text: You seem tense. We don't have to play if it's a lot.

reaction.text: I'm not tense, I'm winning. Which is different. Which you'll learn.
The ear closest to you pins back flat. The other stays up. She's arguing with herself.

desc: A rainy evening: she brings a board game she is sure she will win, and explains the rules in a way that favours her.
